rules.title: Rent control and rent increase limits for covered Hoboken dwellings
rules.requirement: For covered rental housing, rents are controlled at the base rent level, and rent increases are void unless authorized by Chapter 155. At lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy, the landlord may not request or receive more than the lesser of 5% or the applicable CPI percentage differential, and generally may impose no more than one cost-of-living increase in any twelve-month period.
rules.key_value: Lesser of 5% or CPI differential; no more than one cost-of-living increase in any 12-month period

coverage.other_unresolvable: Exempts newly constructed dwellings for the initial rent or lease agreement after first rental, buildings completely vacant on or before and since January 1, 1984 for the initial rent or lease after registration, and multiple dwellings constructed after June 25, 1987 for a period tied to initial mortgage amortization or 30 years, whichever is less, if statutory requirements are met.
coverage.summary: Applies to dwelling units in Hoboken unless an exemption in § 155-2 applies.

rules.exemptions: Motels and hotels; newly constructed dwellings rented for the first time during the initial rent or lease agreement if registered before first rental; industrial property; nonresidential and commercial property, except apartment units in mixed-use buildings; student housing owned or controlled by a school, college or similar institution; housing owned and operated by other government agencies; buildings completely vacant on or before and since January 1, 1984 under stated conditions; and qualifying multiple dwellings constructed after June 25, 1987 during the statutory exemption period.
rules.interaction: The chapter states that when a governmental agency contract preempts Hoboken rent regulation, Chapter 155 is preempted during that agency-regulated period and applies before the contract begins and immediately after it terminates.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.
